comparison.objective: Both set a continuous robot mechanism parameter, secure it without losing the setting, and verify the released result.
comparison.physical_skill: Both require bimanual counterholding during tightening; the candidate uses coaxial driver-and-jam-nut countertorque, while PR-2203 holds a sliding motor plate while tightening two separate bolts.
comparison.success_condition: Both require the target setting to remain after release, secured hardware, stability, tool withdrawal, and clearance; PR-2203 measures belt deflection, while the candidate measures stop angle and repeated-cycle drift.
comparison.reason: The concrete mechanisms differ, but both primarily test preserving a continuous adjustment against fastening reaction and proving the setting after release; repeated jaw cycling adds evidence rather than a clearly separate core ability.
